q: What is the standard SI unit of length?
What type of motion is executed by a swinging pendulum?
What is the standard SI unit of length and its common subdivisions?
a: The SI unit of length is the Meter (m). Subdivisions: 1 m = 100 centimeters (cm); 1 cm = 10 millimeters (mm); 1 kilometer (km) = 1000 m.

q: What is Parallax Error and how can it be avoided during length measurement?
a: Parallax error is line-of-sight misalignment caused by viewing a measurement mark at an angle. It is avoided by positioning the eye directly vertically above the mark being read.

q: Describe how to measure the length of a curved line accurately using a thread.
a: Place a flexible thread carefully along the curved contour marking start and end points with knots, then pull the thread taut along a standard flat meter scale to read the length.

q: Define Rectilinear, Circular, and Periodic motion.
a: Rectilinear Motion: Movement along a straight line. Circular Motion: Movement along a circular path at fixed radius. Periodic Motion: Motion repeating at equal regular time intervals.

q: Give an example of an object exhibiting multiple types of motion simultaneously.
a: A rolling bowling ball or bicycle wheel: it undergoes rotational/circular motion about its center axle while moving forward in rectilinear motion along the ground.
